text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE

- Paper says President Sali Berisha's convoy was shot at as it passed through Lushnje town during an electoral tour. It also says people in Kavaje hurled stones at Berisha's car, although the president's office denies both events.
- Prime Minister Bashkim Fino is under heavy pressure from opposition parties which have threatened to pull out of the government if Fino fails to persuade Berisha to amend the electoral law.
- Italy is stepping up pressure on Albanian politicians to reach consensus on the electoral law so that elections can be held in June as planned.
- Three bridges linking the northern town of Shkoder with the rest of the country have been damaged in explosions.
- A referendum on the monarchy to be held on the same day as parliamentary elections is anti-constitutional, paper says.
ALBANIA
- The European Democratic Union (EDU) will continue to support the Democratic Party on a political and practical level, the EDU fact-finding mission to Albania concluded.
- Turkey will not allow any government to interfere in the domestic affairs of Albania, Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said in a statement.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE

- U.S. Secretary of State Madaleine Albright has turned down a request by Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino for a troika made up of Albright, Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and OSCE envoy Franz Vranitzky to head a mission currently entrusted to Vranitzky.
- Albania's lek currency and its economy have been a sacrificial lamb on the sterile altar of Albanian politics.
- European envoy Franz Vranitzky said he did not plan to visit Tirana this week.
- An earthquake has destroyed 45 houses in south-east Albania, leaving 300 people homeless.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Editorial says the Socialists want to postpone elections because they know they will lose again.
- The bodyguard of the Greek consulate in town of Gjirokaster was found dead on Tuesday. Police said he had committed suicide.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- The editorial says Berisha must go as soon as possible if the current crisis in Albania is to be resolved.
- Two people were shot dead in Shkoder over the weekend.
INDIPENDENT

- Paper publishes full page report on an alleged telephone conversation between Democratic Party chairman Tritan Shehu and Italian ambassador Paolo Foresti, showing that the Italian envoy has given his full support to the Democrats.
